scenes.heading: Recurring decimals to fractions
scenes.say: Your calculator says zero point four five four five, forever. Which fraction made that? Today you will learn a neat trick that makes the endless digits vanish.
scenes.caption: Your calculator says 0.4545…, forever. Which fraction made that? Today you will learn a neat trick that makes the endless digits vanish.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Two endless trains with matching carriages, one slid a carriage along
scenes.science: Shift the decimal one block and subtract: the tail cancels
scenes.breaks: Real trains end, so the last carriages would not match. A recurring decimal never ends, so every digit cancels.
scenes.say: Picture two endless trains with the same pattern on their carriages. Slide one along by exactly one pattern and every carriage lines up. Subtract, and the endless parts cancel. The analogy breaks down because real trains end, but a recurring decimal never does, so every digit after the point cancels perfectly.

scenes.heading: Shift and subtract
scenes.question: Write 0.4̇5̇ as a fraction.
scenes.say: Let x be zero point four five repeating. The block has two digits, so multiply by one hundred. Subtract x, and the tails cancel: ninety-nine x equals forty-five. So x is forty-five over ninety-nine, which simplifies to five elevenths.
scenes.caption: Let x = 0.4545… The block has 2 digits, so multiply by 100. Subtract x and the tails cancel: 99x = 45. So x = 45/99 = 5/11.

scenes.heading: The nines shortcut
points: Number of 9s = digits in the block
scenes.say: When the repeat starts straight after the point, there is a shortcut. Put the repeating block over the same number of nines. One digit, one nine. Two digits, ninety-nine. Then simplify.

scenes.heading: When the repeat starts late
scenes.question: Write 0.83̇ (0.8333…) as a fraction.
scenes.say: In zero point eight three three three, only the three repeats. Multiply by ten so the threes start right after the point, then by one hundred to shift one more block. Subtract: ninety x equals seventy-five, so x is five sixths.
scenes.caption: In 0.8333…, only the 3 repeats. 10x = 8.333…, 100x = 83.333… Subtract: 90x = 75, so x = 5/6.

scenes.heading: Stops or repeats?
scenes.say: Do not mix these up. Zero point seven stops, so it is seven tenths. Zero point seven recurring never stops, so it is seven ninths, which is a little bigger.
scenes.caption: 0.7 stops, so it is 7/10. 0.777… never stops, so it is 7/9, which is a little bigger.

points: Multiply to shift one full block
scenes.say: Quick recap. Call the decimal x, multiply to shift one full repeating block, and subtract so the tail cancels. If the repeat starts late, use one hundred x minus ten x. Simplify, and check by dividing. And yes, zero point nine recurring is exactly one! Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Quick recap. Call the decimal x, multiply to shift one full repeating block, and subtract so the tail cancels. If the repeat starts late, use 100x − 10x. Simplify, and check by dividing. And yes, 0.9̇ is exactly 1! Now try the practice questions!
